def: Spending extra computation on one question at answer time, by sampling, checking and building on candidates, without changing the model's weights.
The fraction of problems for which at least one of n sampled answers is correct, which is the ceiling a perfect selector could reach.
The chance that at least one of k samples for a problem is correct, usually estimated from a larger batch of samples with an unbiased formula.
Sampling n candidate answers and returning the one a selector such as a test suite or verifier ranks highest.
Sampling several reasoning paths and returning the most common final answer.
A checker, exact or learned, that decides whether a candidate answer is correct or how good it is.
A model that scores each intermediate step of a reasoning chain rather than only the final answer.
A prompting and search method in which the model proposes and evaluates partial reasoning steps while a search procedure decides which to extend.
Adaptive-branching Monte Carlo tree search, which at each node chooses between generating a new answer and refining an existing one using Thompson sampling.
The computation spent when a model answers a query, as opposed to the computation spent training it.
